artworks.title: Diomedes and Glaucus Exchanging Armour
artworks.description: Attic red-figure pelike (c. 420 BC, Museo Regionale Archeologico, Gela): Diomedes and the Lycian captain clasp hands and trade armour — gold for bronze — after discovering their grandfathers' guest-friendship (Iliad 6).

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.description: Book 6: Glaucus tells Bellerophon's line and will not fight Diomedes — the armour exchange remains epic's most famous mid-battle truce.

popCulture.title: Glaucus of Lycia
popCulture.description: Son of Hippolochus, peer of Sarpedon — the Lycian who gave gold for bronze and kept guest-friendship above the war.
